metadata.color_semantics: TEAL = honest encoding / correct choice / zero baseline; CRIMSON = misleading encoding / truncated axis / exaggerated effect; GOLD = the structural choice / the argument; SLATE = neutral/gray bars / de-emphasized data

beats.narration_text: Move three: remove the error bars. The uncertainty was real — plus or minus five percentage points. Without error bars, both estimates look precise. The 7-point difference looks definitive. With error bars visible, the confidence intervals overlap: there may be no real difference at all.

beats.narration_text: Visualization is not transparent communication of facts. It is an argument, made through structural choices, about what the facts mean and how the reader should weight them. Engineers undercredit this — and produce many of the most misleading dashboards in deployment without intending to mislead.

beats.narration_text: A product team shares a retention chart at the quarterly review. Month one: eighty-one percent. Month two: eighty-four. Month three: eighty-seven. On the dashboard, the y-axis starts at seventy-nine — the bars shoot up and nearly fill the frame. Every stakeholder in the room describes it as a massive recovery. The CSV shows a six-point improvement over three months. The truncated axis turned a modest gain into a wall.
